checkpoint.resumeInstruction: 1) wugs-s3 is at branch-complete, PR #727 open as DRAFT (https://github.com/heymishy/skills-repo/pull/727) -- not yet merged, no manual pre-merge step required for this story (unlike wugs-s6, it reuses wugs-s6's already-built write adapter rather than adding new real-GitHub-API surface). The operator can merge whenever ready; after merge, write wugs-s3's DoD (same pattern as wugs-s1/s2/s5/s6 -- artefacts/2026-08-11-web-ui-guardrails-standards-surface/dod/wugs-s3-dod.md, gate-advance pipeline-state.json to definition-of-done, commit+push to master). 2) Then continue the inner loop for wugs-s7 (next in the corrected sequence: wugs-s7 -> wugs-s4 -> wugs-s8 -> wugs-s9 -> wugs-s10 -> wugs-s11 -> wugs-s12), following the exact same branch-setup -> implementation-plan -> subagent-execution -> verify-completion -> branch-complete -> DoD cycle used for wugs-s1/s2/s5/s6/s3. 3) Process pattern that worked well this session and should continue: for lock-in tests predicted by the plan to already pass with zero new implementation code, a single implementer dispatch + direct self-verification (git log + running the test + reading the diff) is sufficient -- spinning up separate spec-compliance/code-quality reviewer subagents for a pure test-only diff that matches the plan verbatim is disproportionate. For tasks introducing genuinely new implementation logic, the full implementer -> spec-compliance reviewer -> code-quality reviewer -> fix -> re-review cycle is worth the cost every time -- it caught real Critical security gaps (missing CSRF, missing tenantId validation) that would otherwise have shipped. 4) New pattern discovered this session, apply going forward: this codebase has governed 'enumeration checklist' tests (found so far: check-d2-banner-exit-permission-visibility.js, check-d4-nfr-security-review-and-hardening.js) that hard-count every requireAdmin-gated route and assert an exact allowlist of route path literals -- adding ANY new admin-gated route anywhere in server.js will make these fail by design, and this is NOT a bug to route around; it's a deliberate audit tripwire requiring the checklist to be consciously updated (count bumped, new route added to the allowlist, a route-specific wiring assertion added matching the existing pattern) with the update reflecting a real verification that the new route follows the same wiring convention as every other one. Grep for 'requireAdmin(' before wiring any new admin route in future stories to check whether these checklists need updating. 5) For every pipeline-state.json write: fetch origin/master first and compare against HEAD before writing directly -- if no drift, safe to write directly (true for every write this session). This session's writes were done directly from master (via bin/skills advance/gate-advance run from the main repo root, with the branch-complete artefact JSON copied from the worktree into master's working tree first) rather than from within the worktree -- both approaches are valid per CLAUDE.md, pick whichever is already open. Nested array fields (tasks[N].tddState) still require a direct Edit + immediate check-pipeline-state-integrity.js run, not `skills advance`. Baseline test count to expect throughout: 33 pre-existing failures out of 511 files (documented in decisions.md's repeated RISK-ACCEPT entries) -- confirm this hasn't changed before assuming any new failure is pre-existing.
